proposed.text: An architect installs accessible ramps and an accessible toilet to comply with BP 344. The building owner asks whether this investment yields any tax benefit. Which answer correctly evaluates the situation?

options.text: No tax benefit applies to accessibility improvements since these are mandatory code compliance costs, which are not incentivized
The owner may claim up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs under RA 7277 incentives
The owner receives a 25% tax credit (not deduction) on accessibility improvement costs under RA 10754, which can be applied to future tax liabilities
The owner receives full exemption from real property tax on floors that contain accessible features, significantly reducing tax obligations

proposed.rationale: Up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs is available under RA 7277 incentive provisions and BIR guidance. Beyond normal depreciation, the Philippine law framework — specifically RA 7277 as amended and BIR implementing rules — allows businesses to claim an additional deduction of up to 50% of the direct costs of installing accessibility improvements such as ramps, lifts, and accessible toilets that comply with BP 344. This is distinct from the 25% wage deduction (which applies only to PWD employee salaries). The improvement deduction effectively subsidizes BP 344 compliance by reducing taxable income, making accessibility economically less burdensome.
proposed.explanation: Up to 50% additional deduction on direct accessibility improvement costs effectively subsidizes BP 344 compliance.
